lessons.title: Coordinating the processing operation
lessons.html:
Coordinating the processing operation

Seed arrives at the processing plant from the field with soil, chaff, weed seed, broken and small seed mixed in. Processing turns it into clean, graded, treated and packed seed ready for sale. As a controller you coordinate the people, machines and seed lots so that each lot is processed correctly and kept separate.

The usual processing line

  1. Receiving and sampling
  2. Drying, if moisture is too high
  3. Pre-cleaning (scalping off large trash)
  4. Cleaning on air-screen cleaners
  5. Grading by size and shape (for example maize flat and round grades)
  6. Specific gravity separation to remove light, damaged seed
  7. Seed treatment with registered products
  8. Packing, weighing, labelling and palletising

Planning a run

  • Check the processing order: lot number, crop, cultivar, class, quantity, required grades, treatment and pack size.
  • Confirm that the lot is approved for processing, for example field certification passed.
  • Choose the screens and settings for the crop and lot. Record them.
  • Check that treatment chemicals, bags, labels and pallets are available.
  • Brief the team: who runs each machine, the targets and the safety rules.

Clean-down between lots

Mixing of cultivars is one of the most serious faults in seed processing. Before a new lot, the whole line must be cleaned: elevators, bins, screens, conveyors and the treater. Use compressed air, brushes and inspection hatches. A senior person checks and signs the clean-down sheet. A few seeds of a yellow maize left in a white maize line can lead to customer complaints and rejected lots.

Safety coordination

Confirm that guards are in place, dust extraction is working and lock-out procedures are followed for any maintenance or clearing of blockages. The OHS Act 85 of 1993 requires the employer to provide safe machinery and training; the controller makes sure this happens on the floor.

lessons.title: Monitoring the operation
lessons.html:
Monitoring the operation

Once the line is running, the controller monitors quality, flow and safety. Small problems become big losses if nobody notices them for a few hours.

Quality checks during the run

  • Take samples at set intervals from the cleaner, grader and gravity table outputs.
  • Check for weed seed, broken seed, trash and seed in the wrong grade.
  • Check the reject streams. Too much good seed in rejects means settings are wrong and money is being lost.
  • Check seed treatment coverage: colour should be even and the rate correct according to the product label and treater calibration.
  • Check bag weights on the packing line and that labels show the right lot, cultivar and treatment information.

Flow and machine checks

CheckProblem it shows
Bin levelsBlockage or wrong feed rate
Screen conditionTorn or blinded screens
Unusual noise or vibrationWorn bearings, loose parts
Dust leaksFailed seals or extraction
Elevator speedSlipping belts, seed damage

Seed damage

Seed is alive. Dropping it from height, high elevator speeds and too many handling steps crack seed and lower germination. Watch drop heights and use seed-friendly conveyors where possible.

Responding to problems

  1. Stop the line if quality is out of specification or there is a safety hazard.
  2. Isolate and lock out machines before anyone clears a blockage.
  3. Fix the cause, re-check samples and restart.
  4. Record the problem, the action and the time lost.

People

Check that operators wear hearing protection, dust masks and gloves where required, especially at the treater. Workers handling treated seed must not eat, drink or smoke on the line and must wash before breaks.

lessons.title: Completing the processing operation
lessons.html:
Completing the processing operation

At the end of a lot or a shift the controller closes off the run properly. This makes the seed traceable and prepares the line for the next lot.

Closing a lot

  • Weigh and record all outputs: packed seed per grade, rejects, screenings and dust.
  • Calculate the processing yield: packed seed as a percentage of incoming weight. Compare with expected yield and explain big differences.
  • Take the official final sample from the packed lot for laboratory tests (purity, germination, moisture) as procedure requires.
  • Place the packed lot in quarantine until laboratory results approve it for sale.

Handling by-products

Rejects and screenings must be handled according to company procedure. Treated seed and treated rejects must never be sold as food or animal feed. They are disposed of as the treatment product label and waste procedures require.

Clean-down and housekeeping

  1. Clean the line fully for the next lot and sign the clean-down sheet.
  2. Clean the treater and store chemicals in the locked chemical store.
  3. Sweep floors and remove dust, which is a fire and explosion hazard in seed plants.
  4. Report any maintenance needed.

Records and reporting

RecordUse
Processing order and settingsRepeat good results next time
Quality check resultsProof of control
Yields and lossesCosting and improvement
Treatment product, batch and rateTraceability and safety
Clean-down sign-offProof against cultivar mixing

Report the shift results to the plant manager: what was processed, problems, downtime and any quality issues. Good records allow a complaint months later to be traced to the exact lot, machine and shift.

Key points

  • Plan each run from the processing order and confirm the lot is approved.
  • Clean the whole line between lots and sign it off to prevent mixing.
  • Sample outputs and rejects regularly and stop the line when out of specification.
  • Lock out machines before clearing blockages.
  • Treated seed is never sold as food or feed; record everything for traceability.
